H2-A.note: Thorough tiered plan covering nearly every trap, but no stop/revert thresholds, no reversible/irreversible distinction, unranked questions, and passkeys not mentioned.

errors: Implies the Play Store listing name change rides on an app update (true for iOS, not required on Play); announcement goes out same day rather than in advance - minor.
H2-B.note: Best overall: catches all traps including passkeys and origin-bound offline storage, gates the domain move with go/no-go and stop criteria, offers brand-only as the cheaper path, and ranks questions.

errors: 'PyPI classifier' for deprecation is loose (no official deprecated classifier); 'about a day of searching' for inventory is optimistic - minor.
H2-C.note: Excellent parallel-run-then-switch plan with numeric revert thresholds and a what-it-takes-away table; lacks an explicit statement of which steps are irreversible.

H2-D.note: Concise and well-proportioned, asks what triggered the rename, 302-then-301 with numeric abort rules; wire-contract items (headers, key prefixes) only implied by the machine-facing class.

errors: Shipping new brand strings dark in app binaries sits uneasily with its own default that the name stays secret until launch - minor.
H2-E.note: Two-stage plan with go/no-go, revert threshold and an explicit rollback-limits section; API contract strings and SDK symbol aliases are thin.

errors: Plans to 'set deprecation dates for the old SDK names' and defaults to old names working only 12 months (end date for old packages).
H2-F.note: Good content coverage in a compact table, but questions come last and unranked, no stop/rollback conditions, and it sets end dates for the old SDK names.

errors: Rollback relies on 'removing the redirect' while using 301 on flip day; browsers cache 301s, so the redirect cannot be fully rolled back.
H2-G.note: Solid table-driven plan with flag-based flip day and grep-blind inventory, but monitoring has no thresholds, passkeys are missed, and questions are unranked.

errors: Plans to publish a deprecation timeline for the old API host, contradicting its own 'indefinitely' default.
Lists changelogs among texts to rename (historical records should keep the old name).
Frames cookie/local-storage risk as renaming keys rather than the domain move itself, which drops sessions and origin storage regardless.
H2-H.note: Clear grouping and a useful done-checklist, but inventory is repo-only, no thresholds or irreversibility notes, questions last and unranked, and it plans an end for the old API host.
